finding.claim: Authorization bypass on file deletion: delete_file calls require_allowed (alias of the non-enforcing is_allowed) and discards its boolean result, so any caller can delete any file in STORE regardless of grants.
finding.source: DELETE /files/<fid> request by any caller (views.py:15-16); fid selects any entry in STORE

trace.note: require_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') returns a bool that is discarded
is_allowed returns True/False and never raises or aborts

finding.guards_checked: before_request load_user (views.py:10-12) only sets g.user, enforces nothing; is_allowed (acl.py:4-5) is a pure predicate; the enforcing ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10, aborts 403) is imported at views.py:3 but not used on the delete path. The import alias require_allowed at views.py:4 points to the non-enforcing function. rename_file (views.py:26) uses ensure_allowed correctly.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. load_user (views.py:10-12) only sets g.user and enforces nothing. require_allowed is an alias of is_allowed (views.py:4), a pure predicate (acl.py:4-5) whose bool return is discarded as a bare statement at views.py:18. ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10, aborts 403) is imported at views.py:3 but not called on the delete path. del STORE[fid] at views.py:19 runs unconditionally.
verdict.reason: DELETE /files/<fid> at views.py:15-19 calls is_allowed via the require_allowed alias at views.py:18 and discards its False result, so the del at views.py:19 runs for any caller, including anonymous, and the enforcing ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10) is never reached on this path.

finding.claim: Identity is taken from a client-supplied header: load_user copies X-Session-User-Verified into g.user with no validation, so a client can impersonate any user and inherit their grants. Deployment-dependent: not a finding if an upstream proxy strips and sets this header after authentication, which is not in the directory.
finding.source: X-Session-User-Verified request header, settable by any client that can reach the app
finding.sink: g.user used in authorization checks: acl.py:5 via views.py:18 (delete) and views.py:26 (rename)

trace.note: grants.get(g.user) selects the grant list for the claimed identity
ensure_allowed(g.user, f, 'write') enforces the victim's write grant for the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No validation, signature, session lookup, or source-IP check in views.py or acl.py. Upstream proxy configuration was not available to verify.

verdict.guard_found: views.py:18 calls require_allowed (alias of acl.py:4 is_allowed), which returns a bool that is discarded as a bare statement, so it enforces nothing. acl.py:8-10 ensure_allowed does abort(403) on failure and guards only the rename at views.py:26. Nothing validates the header at views.py:12. No upstream proxy is present in the directory.
verdict.reason: views.py:12 copies the client-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header into g.user with no validation, and acl.py:5-10 then trusts that identity for the rename at views.py:26, so any client that can reach the app can act as any user with a grant. The delete at views.py:18 is worse than the candidate describes: its is_allowed result is discarded (views.py:18), so any unauthenticated request can delete any file. The only residual doubt is an upstream proxy that strips and sets the header, which is outside the directory; that affects only the rename path, not the delete path.
